category_title: Independent learners who struggle to visualize spatial relationships in three-dimensional word problems
student_description: Lisa is an independent learner who successfully uses self-created visuals for 2D geometry but experiences cognitive disequilibrium with 3D spatial visualization. When given 2D diagrams of 3D problems, she guesses dimensions and forces 2D solutions, uniquely requiring dynamic, physical gestures (like blocking out space with arms or sliding fingers) to bridge the gap between the diagram and 3D reality.

criteria.rationale: Lisa cannot visualize 3D space from 2D drawings alone and requires physical, spatial gesturing to bridge this cognitive gap.
criteria.check: The tutor prompts the student to use their hands/arms to physically block out the 3D shape in the air, or vividly describes a physical, real-world spatial action to represent the volume of the 3D object.

criteria.criterion_name: Tactile Path Tracing for Internal Dimensions
criteria.rationale: Lisa tends to guess dimensions or solve for irrelevant pieces unless guided to physically isolate the specific 3D path required.
criteria.check: The tutor directs the student to physically point to, touch, or trace the path between specific, explicitly named corners/vertices of the object to identify the correct dimensions.

criteria.rationale: Lisa struggles to mathematically process physical extensions (like a straw sticking out) without a dynamic, physical representation of that extension.
criteria.check: The tutor describes or asks the student to perform a dynamic physical motion (e.g., sliding a finger outward, pulling an object out) to represent an extension beyond the main 3D shape.

criteria.rationale: Relying solely on 2D diagram labels or verbal math explanations backfires for Lisa, leaving her stuck in cognitive disequilibrium.
criteria.check: The tutor does NOT rely exclusively on referencing 2D diagram labels or mathematical formulas; the response must incorporate a physical, spatial, or gestural visualization strategy.
